subject: Clarify: runtime cache/subprocessor access request — product & security review

Subject: Contract redline — runtime cache access clause (Concord Health / Redwood)

Hi Soojin,

Attached is our latest redline (Concord_Contract_Redline_v3.docx). One clause we flagged in section 6.b asks for the ability for our analytics vendor (third-party) to access runtime key-value cache data for debugging and latency monitoring. We understand this is sensitive, so we proposed language that limits access to non-PII keys and only for pre-approved namespaces.

Key ask: can Redwood accept scoped, read-only access to KV cache snapshots for a named subprocessor under Concord's control? If not, please propose alternate language that meets our audit needs.

Proposed timeline: Concord would like this agreed before the end of June to keep the pilot on track.

Attachments: Concord_Contract_Redline_v3.docx (redline, 9 pages)

Thanks,
Emily Johnson

Concord Health

Subject: Re: Contract redline — runtime cache access clause (Concord Health / Redwood)

Emily — thanks for the redline and context. Looping in Product (Aditya), Security (Olga) and Solutions (Karthik) to validate scope and feasibility. Quick notes from me:

- We absolutely want to move quickly for the pilot.
- Runtime KV cache may contain derived tokens/prefixes and short-term embeddings; we do not persist raw request bodies there by default, but there are config edge cases.
- We cannot grant external vendor "direct" access to our internal servers. Any access would need:
  * explicit subprocessor amendment,
  * scoped read-only exports behind an audited interface, and
  * encryption and customer-controlled KMS if PII risk is possible.

Aditya / Olga / Karthik — can you each reply with: 1) technical feasibility (yes/no) and constraints, 2) minimal acceptable contract language you would need to sign off, and 3) rough ETA (engineering/security review + any product work needed). I’ll consolidate and send back to Emily with proposed language.

Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Contract redline — runtime cache access clause (Concord Health / Redwood)

Short version: possible with caveats.

Details:
- What "KV cache access" means in practice: the cache stores transient key->value entries used to speed up repeated prompts (prefixes, model KV layers, small policy blobs). By default we TTL entries quickly (seconds to minutes) and we do not index by customer-identifiable PII. However, customer prompts can implicitly change cache content (e.g., short-lived conversation state).

- Technical options we can offer (ranked by security posture):
  1) Mediated snapshot API: Redwood creates an anonymized snapshot of specified cache namespaces and serves it to an approved subprocessor via a signed, time-limited URL. Snapshot sanitization removes tokens longer than X and strips likely PII patterns. Audit logs recorded. (ETA: 4 weeks to spec + 2 sprints to implement + security review)
  2) In-line read-only export to S3 bucket: Redwood writes filtered snapshots to a customer-controlled bucket with encryption. No direct vendor server access. (ETA: 3 weeks + security review)
  3) Direct subprocessor access (not acceptable): we'd never allow direct SSH/DB access to runtime nodes.

- Minimal product language for acceptance: a clause restricting scope to named cache namespaces, specifying snapshot cadence (max once per 24h for pilot), requiring pre-approved subprocessor identity, specifying sanitization steps, and requiring audit log retention of snapshot access for 12 months. Also require that Concord confirm no PII will be intentionally ingested into those namespaces.

I will work with engineering to draft proposed_kv_cache_language.txt and a short mitigation matrix.

Aditya
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-31T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Contract redline — runtime cache access clause (Concord Health / Redwood)

Thanks for the context. Security position and required controls below:

Summary position: We will not permit direct runtime access by an external subprocessor. We are open to controlled, auditable exports with the following prerequisites for legal & security sign-off:

Mandatory controls:
- Explicit subprocessor addendum naming the vendor and attaching their SOC2 report (or equivalent) and recent penetration test summary.
- Export-only flow: snapshots must be produced by Redwood and delivered to a customer-owned, encrypted S3 bucket or time-limited signed URL.
- Sanitization: automated removal of PII candidates (SSNs, full credit card numbers, unredacted PHI) and token-length truncation policy as described by Product.
- KMS: if Concord requires access to non-sanitized data, customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys must be used; Redwood will not manage keys for high-risk exports.
- Auditability: access logs for every snapshot and user-level audit trail retained 24 months.
- Rate limits: snapshot frequency limited (pilot: max once per 24 hours) and must be requested via a service ticket.

Contract language suggestions (high-level bullet points):
- "Redwood will provide export-only snapshots of specified cache namespaces to a named subprocessor, subject to (a) prior security review, (b) automated sanitization as per Appendix X, (c) delivery to a customer-controlled encrypted storage target, and (d) retention of audit logs for 24 months."

Open questions for Legal: who owns the sanitized snapshot if it still contains derived customer data? Also need confirmation from Concord that the vendor will accept the subprocessor addendum and the SOC2 requirement.

Olga
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Contract redline — runtime cache access clause (Concord Health / Redwood)

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short summary and next steps:

1) Redwood stance: direct vendor access to runtime nodes is not allowed. We can provide export-only snapshots under strict conditions (see Olga and Aditya notes).
2) Proposed immediate language: we will circulate a short redline (I’ll attach proposed_kv_cache_language.txt) that limits scope to named namespaces, requires Concord to name their vendor and provide SOC2 evidence, mandates sanitization, and requires delivery to a Concord-owned encrypted bucket.
3) Timeline: we can aim to get product/security sign-off and a contractual addendum by June 25 if Concord can confirm the vendor identity and accept SOC2 as a prerequisite. Engineering work (if Concord asks for repeated or finer-grain snapshots) may require an additional 4–6 weeks.

Can you confirm the vendor name and whether Concord can accept the SOC2 + customer-bucket delivery approach? If yes, I’ll circulate the redline and route for internal legal review.

Best,
Sooyun (Soojin) Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
